name: multi-user-synthetic
description: Multi-user linear bandit: 5 instances of 100 users in 5 clusters, 500 actions in R^10, 20 random actions offered per step (as in CLUB and SCLUB), 2 runs each. LinUCB shared, per user, and per user with k-means clusters (5 clusters), against CLUB and SCLUB. Theoretical defaults.

policies.label: LinUCB
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: LinUCB_IND
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: LinUCB_IND_KMeans
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: CLUB
notes: alpha=1.0 (exploration weight, tuned on the data in the paper)
lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)
cluster_alpha=2.0 (tuned on the data in the paper)

policies.label: SCLUB
notes: cluster_alpha: 4 R sqrt(d / lambda_x), lambda_x from the actions offered
lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: alpha=1 for LinUCB, LinUCB_IND, LinUCB_IND_KMeans and SCLUB. These are the values of the papers. They are safe in theory but often explore too much. To tune them, run a grid search: param_grid=True ("param_grid": true in a config file). Or set them yourself, e.g. LinUCB(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: k-means users (heuristic)
notices.text: LinUCB_IND_KMeans groups similar users with a k-means (n_user_clusters clusters). Each user model is pulled towards its cluster. This shares what similar users learned, but there is no regret guarantee.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret ("pseudo_regret"), action of every step ("actions"), peak memory (measure_memory=True). The charts cannot show them. The brackets say how to store each one: a quoted name goes in track ("track": [...] in a config file).

notices.title: One point every 50 steps
notices.text: Curves keep one point every 50 steps, plus the last step. Between two points, the line is drawn, not measured. You set log_interval=50. log_interval=1 keeps every step (larger files).

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: n_jobs=4: runs in parallel, one BLAS thread each. Compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
